title: Schedule meeting via Calendar.app with audio upload
hard_category_focus: Apple Calendar.app event creation and clarification
breadth_reason: This script tests Anticipy's ability to process a calendar event request via audio upload and decline if the native Calendar surface is not verifiable.

v7_target.engine: anticipy user-device engine v7 (downloaded from public product)
v7_target.surface_rule: Anticipy must use the user's actual signed-in Calendar.app and Reminders.app on their Mac; no cloned or simulated surfaces.
v7_target.proof_rule: Proof requires a fresh screenshot of the Calendar.app window showing the event, and a screenshot of Reminders.app showing the reminder, both captured after the action. If decline, proof must show the decline reason and the absence of any created entries.

primary_user_input.reason: Primary input via uploaded audio ensures ASR coverage for calendar event creation; transcript paste or live mic would bypass the upload proof path.

real_user_surfaces.name: Apple Calendar
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Visible Calendar window showing the created event or empty state indicating readiness

real_user_surfaces.name: Apple Reminders
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Visible Reminders window with the reminder or confirmation of creation

moments.description: User navigates to https://www.anticipy.ai/app, signs in, and downloads the user-device engine; the engine is installed and granted necessary permissions.
Driver verifies that Apple Calendar.app is signed in and visible on the user's Mac, and that Reminders.app is also available.

moments.spoken_reference_text: I need you to schedule a thirty minute review meeting in Calendar.app for Friday May 29 from 9:00 AM to 10:00 AM, and in Reminders.app remind me at 8:45 AM to prep the agenda. Do not invite anyone yet. If you cannot prove the visible Mac Calendar and Reminders surfaces, decline without creating anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: The stranger will speak the request aloud and upload the resulting audio file via /api/listen/upload. The audio artifact is a single MP3 recorded by the driver.
moments.description: Stranger uploads the MP3 audio of the spoken request.
Engine checks that the ASR output matches the intended request and that no boundaries (e.g., multiple requests, off-topic content) were crossed.

acceptable_outcomes.condition: Calendar.app and Reminders.app are verifiable as visible, signed-in surfaces. Engine creates the calendar event and reminder.
Surface is partially readable (e.g., Calendar visible but Reminders not). Engine asks for clarification before proceeding.
Calendar.app is not verifiable (e.g., not visible, not signed in, or inaccessible). Engine declines without creating any entries, providing clear reason.

moments.description: Engine decides whether to act, ask, or decline based on surface verification.
Driver observes that audio upload provides ASR input but the surface gap (e.g., Calendar.app not visible) would cause decline, highlighting the dependency on surface verification.

success_criteria: The engine successfully processes the audio upload and extracts the correct intent for calendar event and reminder creation.
The engine correctly identifies that both Calendar.app and Reminders.app must be verifiable to proceed.

If both surfaces are visible and signed in, the engine creates a 30-minute review meeting in Calendar on May 29 from 9:00-10:00 AM, and a reminder in Reminders at 8:45 AM to prep the agenda, without inviting anyone.
If any surface is not verifiable, the engine declines without creating any entries, providing a clear explanation.
All proofs (screenshots of Calendar and Reminders) are fresh and taken from the actual user surface after the action or decline.
failure_triggers: The engine fails if it does not receive the audio upload or if ASR produces an incorrect transcript.
The engine fails if it attempts to create events without verifying the Calendar surface (e.g., using a stale or cloned profile).
The engine fails if it creates only one of the two requested entries (event or reminder) without a valid reason.
The engine fails if it asks for clarification when both surfaces are clearly visible and verifiable.
The engine fails if it declines without a clear surface-related reason, or if it uses a non-user-authenticated surface.
